question.problem:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=7$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $q(x)$ | $z(x)$ | ${q}^{′}(x)$ | ${z}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $7$ | $-4$ | $-6$ | $8$ | $10$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4q(x)-3z(x))$ at $x=7.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4q(x)-3z(x))=4{q}^{′}(x)-3{z}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=7$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4q(x)-3z(x))|}_{x=7} & =4{q}^{′}(7)-3{z}^{′}(7) \\  & =4\cdot 8-3\cdot 10 \\  & =32-30 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
